Budgets.description:
Caps the executor enforces out-of-process.

``cost_units`` travels with the run so a provider can report against it, but
RP-0 enforces only the two caps it can enforce locally: wall clock and output
size. Cost enforcement belongs to the metering substrate.
Budgets.title: Budgets

ContractRef.description:
A pin to one Contract version.

Operations write ``name@N``; the install pins each to the digest of the copy
the package carries. A carried Contract pins every nested Contract by digest.
ContractRef.title: ContractRef

ImplementationManifest.description: One entrypoint inside a provider package: how and where it runs.
ImplementationManifest.title: ImplementationManifest

ContractRef.description:
A pin to one Contract version.

Operations write ``name@N``; the install pins each to the digest of the copy
the package carries. A carried Contract pins every nested Contract by digest.
ContractRef.title: ContractRef

OperationRefusal.description:
One typed refusal an operation may return: its detail Contract.

``absorbable`` declares that the refusal means "this input is unavailable",
which a Line acquisition rule may absorb instead of failing the run.
OperationRefusal.title: OperationRefusal

BuiltAgainstCapability.description: One capability version the package's copies were made from.
BuiltAgainstCapability.title: BuiltAgainstCapability

BuiltAgainstCaptureKind.description: One CaptureKind a carried copy was made from, by the digest of its declared copy.
BuiltAgainstCaptureKind.title: BuiltAgainstCaptureKind

CarriedCaptureKind.description:
A CaptureKind the operations name: its name, decoding and layout, as core declares them.

A raw kind may carry neither (the operation names it without promising a
document shape). A layout needs a JSON or CSV decoding.
CarriedCaptureKind.title: CarriedCaptureKind

CarriedContract.description:
One Contract the package carries, as a full ``cruxible-contract-v1`` document.

The runtime reads its identity and the Contracts and kinds its field types
name; core judges the rest (types, refinements, digests).
CarriedContract.title: CarriedContract

Operations write ``name@N``; the install pins each to the digest of the copy
the package carries. A carried Contract pins every nested Contract by digest.
ContractRef.title: ContractRef

OperationSource.description:
Where an operation's code is.

``path`` is relative to the root of ``repository`` (or, for a local build
with no repository, to the provider's project directory). ``revision`` is
the full commit id the build was made from, and needs ``repository``.
OperationSource.title: OperationSource

ProviderDeclares.description:
The shapes a package carries for its operations; never installed as instance state.

``contracts`` are sorted by name then version, ``capture_kinds`` by name,
``built_against`` by kind, name, then version; each is listed once.
ProviderDeclares.title: ProviderDeclares

ProviderOperation.description:
One operation a provider package serves (registration schema 3).

``serves`` lists capability names, sorted and once each, at most sixteen,
none under ``workspace.``: fit is checked against whichever version a slot
pins. ``may_truncate``: the operation may return a truncated listing, so it
binds only a slot that declares ``may_truncate`` too.
ProviderOperation.title: ProviderOperation

ResourceRef.description: A package file the registration names, by package-relative path and sha256.
ResourceRef.title: ResourceRef

RuntimeRequirement.description:
Something an implementation's environment needs beyond its lock.

Keyed by the manifest implementation it belongs to: its ``entrypoint``.
RuntimeRequirement.title: RuntimeRequirement

PackageRegistration.description:
``registration.json``, schema 3, exactly as a package ships it.

``manifest`` names the package's runtime manifest by path and digest;
``operations`` are sorted by name, once each; ``declares`` carries every
shape they reach and nothing else.
PackageRegistration.title: PackageRegistration

ProviderErrorPayload.description: A provider-reported failure (an attempted answer that did not succeed).
ProviderErrorPayload.title: ProviderErrorPayload

DistributionRef.description:
Names the distribution this manifest belongs to.

The distribution's own sha256 is deliberately absent: a manifest shipped
inside an artifact cannot contain that artifact's hash. The hash is carried
by the accepted Provider artifact and is what the implementation digest
consumes.
DistributionRef.title: DistributionRef

Refusal.description:
A typed refusal, serialisable into receipts and result envelopes.

``code`` is either one of the runtime's :class:`RefusalCode` values or a
code the bound operation declares. Which one is decided by the spelling,
because the two vocabularies are disjoint.
Refusal.title: Refusal

Trace.description:
Trace material destined for exhaust.

``endpoints_contacted`` is what was *actually* contacted, recorded by the
instrumented client locally and by the proxy log in cloud. It is compared
against the accepted declaration; a contacted endpoint outside the
declaration is a typed conformance violation attributed to the
implementation digest.
Trace.title: Trace

SecretChannelSpec.description: Where the provider process reads credential material from.
SecretChannelSpec.title: SecretChannelSpec

SecretRef.description:
Names a credential without carrying it.

Only the ref travels in the serialised run context. The material arrives
separately over the inherited descriptor named by :class:`SecretChannelSpec`.
SecretRef.title: SecretRef

RunContext.description:
Everything the executor passes into a provider process.

``operation`` is the one operation this run executes, by name;
``operation_signature_digest`` is the exact ``{in, out, effect}`` signature
the Line bound it under; ``build_digest`` is the accepted provider build.
``entrypoint`` is the object the child dispatches to, and it must declare
``operation`` among the operations it serves.
